rv.q: It is an intensely memorable night of theatre.

This is top-drawer stuff, with a leading character drawn from a little-known hero in history and directed with a gentle undercurrent of humor even while educating the audience about a very dark chapter in Europe during WWII.
Garbo is a head-spinning thriller that blends history and humor with the writer’s unabashed love and respect for theater.

Mired by director Carlos Celdrán's initially static blocking, on Jessica Cancino's handsome but sparse set, that narrative setup serves as a stodgy intro for what turns out to be a fascinating chapter of little-known history.
Ultimately, it makes for a fun wartime romp that teeters the line between humor and stress very well.
